mutations.name: control-is-the-subject-restated
mutations._mechanism: The control is detached at HEAD instead of the base: both sides run the same tree, every failure reads BOTH, and a change's own failure is reported as pre-existing (HemaSuite 2026-09-16: two readings through one instrument agree).

mutations.name: a-fail-in-any-run-is-deterministic
mutations._mechanism: The subject's always-failing set becomes its ever-failing set, so a flake that failed once is attributed to the change as NEW.
mutations.find: s_always = set.intersection(*(set(run) for run in subject_runs))
mutations.replace: s_always = set.union(*(set(run) for run in subject_runs))

mutations.name: repeat-is-ignored
mutations._mechanism: Only one run per side happens whatever --repeat says: a flake is read once and lands in an attributed set.

mutations.name: a-flake-hides-a-new-failure
mutations._mechanism: FLAKY outranks NEW: a real new failure beside a pre-existing flake reads as merely flaky.
mutations.replace:
if subject_only and not flaky:
        verdict = "NEW"

mutations.name: control-left-behind
mutations._mechanism: The throwaway worktree is never removed: every invocation leaks a registered worktree and a checkout beside the subject.
mutations.find: removed = _remove_control(subject, control, admin[0] if admin else None)

mutations.name: cleanup-prunes-the-whole-repo
mutations._mechanism: Cleanup ends with a repo-wide `git worktree prune`, which also drops the registration of another session's worktree whose directory is absent at that moment.

mutations.name: sigterm-skips-cleanup
mutations._mechanism: SIGTERM is not turned into an exception, so the process dies at the default action with no finally: the control worktree and its registration are left behind.

mutations.name: busy-session-not-named
mutations._mechanism: A session refused by the tree lock is not recognised as SUITE: BUSY; it falls through to a generic exit reason and the caller cannot tell 'wait for the holder' from a broken run.

mutations.name: crash-not-named
mutations._mechanism: A run killed by a signal is not called crashed.

mutations.name: interrupted-collection-scored
mutations._mechanism: An Interrupted collection is scored: its ERROR <file> line becomes a failure id and the comparison reads FIXED_ONLY instead of cannot-judge.

mutations.name: odd-exit-scored
mutations._mechanism: Exit codes other than 0/1 are not refused by name; a usage error is reported by whatever the output happens to lack.
mutations.find: if rc is not None and rc not in (0, 1):

mutations.name: no-summary-reads-as-no-failures
mutations._mechanism: A log cut off before its summary yields an empty failure set: a killed run reads as 'no failures'.
mutations.find:
if summary is None:
        raise Unreadable("no-summary")
mutations.replace:
if summary is None:
        return {}, None

mutations.name: partial-set-accepted
mutations._mechanism: FAILED lines that disagree with the summary count are accepted: an incomplete set is diffed as if it were whole.
mutations.find: if len(failed) != summary.failed or len(errors) != summary.errors:

mutations.name: exit-code-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A session that exits 1 with no failure listed reads as clean.
mutations.find: if rc is not None and (rc == 1) != bool(failed or errors):

mutations.name: captured-output-read-as-failures
mutations._mechanism: The whole log is scanned, so a FAILED line a test printed in its captured output is taken as one of this run's failures.
mutations.find: for line in tail if starts else []:

mutations.name: greedy-parametrize-id
mutations._mechanism: The bracket group is greedy and swallows a ' - message' that holds brackets into the node id, so the id never matches the control's.

mutations.name: disjoint-roots-diffed
mutations._mechanism: Two readings collected from different roots share no id and are diffed anyway: every failure reads NEW.
mutations.find: if sets["run"] and sets["control"] and not set(sets["run"]) & set(sets["control"]):

mutations.name: id-list-control-refused
mutations._mechanism: A stored baseline_failures.txt id list is parsed as a pytest log and refused as no-summary.

mutations.name: M1-exit-first-read-as-complete
mutations._mechanism: A `-x`/`--maxfail` run's FAILED set is a prefix; read as whole it reports SAME while the new failure behind the first one was never reached.

mutations.name: M1-stopped-log-read-as-complete
mutations._mechanism: Same hole in logs mode: a stored -x log is diffed as a complete set.
mutations.replace: if _STOPPED_RE.search(tail_text) and rc is not None:

mutations.name: M2-handler-raises-into-cleanup
mutations._mechanism: The signal handler raises asynchronously, so a SIGTERM during cleanup aborts the removal: the control leaks and a traceback is the last line.

mutations.name: M3-pythonpath-not-rebased
mutations._mechanism: An absolute PYTHONPATH into the subject reaches the control unchanged: the control imports the subject's code and the two readings agree.

mutations.name: M3-subject-on-control-path-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A .pth (editable-install shape) puts the subject on the control's sys.path and the run goes ahead, measuring the subject twice.

mutations.name: M4-errors-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Per-test ERROR ids are dropped from the set: a change that breaks a fixture reads SAME.
mutations.find: return {node: "+".join(sorted(kind)) for node, kind in kinds.items()}, summary
mutations.replace: return {node: "+".join(sorted(kind)) for node, kind in kinds.items() if "FAILED" in kind}, summary

mutations.name: S1-sides-run-in-parallel
mutations._mechanism: The control's pytest starts while the subject's is running: two sessions race on the shared /tmp sweep and manufacture failures.
mutations.find:
try:
                reason, rc, output = _run_one(argv, root, envs[side], args.timeout, log)

mutations.name: S2-kind-change-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A test that FAILED on the base and ERRORs on the subject reads BOTH: the change's new breakage is filed as pre-existing.
mutations.find: changed = {node: pair for node, pair in changed.items() if all(pair) and pair[0] != pair[1]}

mutations.name: S3-no-subject-repo-reads-SAME
mutations._mechanism: A subject that is not a repository returns a pass exit with no token.

mutations.name: S3-worktree-add-failure-reads-SAME
mutations._mechanism: A control worktree that failed to create returns a pass exit with no token.

mutations.name: S3-timeout-not-named
mutations._mechanism: A hung run is killed and then read as a crash, not as a timeout.

mutations.name: S3-leaked-control-not-reported
mutations._mechanism: A control that could not be removed leaves the comparison token as the last line.

mutations.name: S6-only-the-direct-child-killed
mutations._mechanism: Only pytest itself is killed; what it started keeps running against a deleted control.

mutations.name: S4-output-not-flushed
mutations._mechanism: Output is block-buffered: a caller killed mid-run never saw the CONTROL: path it would need to clean up.

mutations.name: S5-run-log-not-kept
mutations._mechanism: The run's output is discarded, so an attributed id cannot be investigated without a rerun.

mutations.name: N2-banner-searched-in-captured-output
mutations._mechanism: The Interrupted: banner is searched over the whole log, so one a test printed reads as a collection error.

mutations.name: N3-all-skipped-misnamed
mutations._mechanism: An all-skipped selection is reported as no-tests-ran.
mutations.find: raise Unreadable("all-skipped" if "skipped" in summary.phrases else "no-tests-ran")

mutations.name: N4-help-hides-the-root
mutations._mechanism: --help does not say the selection is relative to the toplevel, so a subdirectory-relative selection fails as a usage error.
mutations.find: relative to the subject's toplevel (pytest runs there)")

mutations.name: R2-M1-in-tree-venv-refused
mutations._mechanism: The interpreter's own prefix is not exempt: an in-tree .venv's site-packages reads as the subject's code and every in-tree-venv repo is refused.
mutations.find: and not any(_under(real, prefix) for prefix in prefixes):

mutations.name: R2-S1-pep660-finder-unseen
mutations._mechanism: A PEP 660 editable finder maps the package to the subject with no sys.path entry: the control imports the subject and both sides agree.
mutations.find: leaked += [path for path, text in found["hooks"] if any(name in text for name in names)]

mutations.name: R2-S2-kind-flip-attributed
mutations._mechanism: A failure whose kind flips across a side's runs is compared as a kind change and attributed NEW instead of FLAKY.

mutations.name: R2-N1-log-dir-misnamed
mutations._mechanism: An uncreatable --log-dir is reported as a control-dir failure.

mutations.name: R2-N2-spawn-race-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A signal between Popen and tracking the child is recorded but pytest is not killed; the run waits it out.
mutations.find:
if _STATE["stop"] is not None:   # a signal between Popen and the line above
        _kill_group(proc)

mutations.name: R2-N3-reconfigure-unguarded
mutations._mechanism: main() calls reconfigure on any stdout, so an in-process caller with a StringIO stdout crashes.

mutations.name: R2-probe-failure-read-as-clean
mutations._mechanism: An unreadable import probe is taken as 'imports nothing from the subject' and the run goes ahead.

mutations.name: R3-prefix-exemption-swallows-the-subject
mutations._mechanism: An interpreter prefix that CONTAINS the subject (a repo under a conda env or venv directory) is still exempt, so every subject path on sys.path, an editable .pth included, is exempt and the run reads a false SAME.
